Thanks for routing, Aditya. I pulled the k8s events and control-plane logs for the window Sanjay called out. Short summary:

- 02:18:12 UTC: orchestrator leader election timeout in node-3; leader re-election took ~14s.
- 02:18:28 UTC: agent health-checks began to spike their retry backoffs due to a transient firewall rule applied by the customer's orchestrator upgrade job (we observed SYN-RST clusters in the pcap).
- 02:19:00–02:24:15 UTC: combo of re-election and agent reconnect storms caused a backlog in the control-plane request queue; requests started returning 503 when queue depth exceeded the soft-limit.

Actions taken during/after: rollback of the orchestrator version, temporary relaxation of agent backoff windows by the agent fleet, and an emergency leader-election tuning applied to the manager. The cluster stabilized by ~02:36 UTC.

We recommend the following immediate mitigations to avoid recurrence during future orchestrator upgrades:
1) Add a pre-upgrade gate to drain agent connections in a controlled fashion (agent-side coordinated drain).
2) Harden leader-election timeouts for upgrade windows (tunable via config flag).
3) Operator checklist entry to avoid concurrent firewall rule updates during rolling orchestrator changes.

Priyom
Senior Software Engineer, Servicing Runtime

Hi all — thanks for the productive bridge earlier. Summary and immediate artifacts:

Summary of what we agreed on the bridge:
- Root cause (prelim): orchestrator leader-election lag triggered by concurrent firewall/routing changes from the upgrade job, amplified by agent reconnection storms. The combination briefly overwhelmed control-plane queueing.
- Immediate mitigations agreed: coordinated agent drain prior to orchestrator restarts; temporary leader-election tuning; and a new pre-upgrade check to block firewall/routing changes during the window.
- RCA ETA: 2027-04-08. Toggle ETA: 2027-04-12. Runbook PR: target 2027-04-05.

Artifacts uploaded to Drive: sanitized-manager-logs-02-18-utc.txt, k8s_events_20270328.log, pcap_sample_mediconnect.pcap

Action owners: Priyom (forensics + tuning) / Mina (runbook + checklist PR) / Aditya (customer comms + timeline) / Ben (credits estimate).

We’ll circulate the RCA draft when ready and include a small set of artifacts for your internal postmortem. If Medisync would like, Redwood can also propose a follow-up joint run of the upgrade in a staging window to validate the toggle behavior.

Mina Haddad
Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
